notes: Raspberry Pi is not in the catalogue, so a new 'raspberry-pi' type with the 40-pin header was created. GND pins are numbered GND.1-GND.8 in physical pin order (6, 9, 14, 20, 25, 30, 34, 39). The GND wire goes to physical pin 9, which is GND.2.

The breadboard catalogue uses bank 't' for rows a-e and 'b' for rows f-j. The photo draws rows f-j at the top, so the buttons and their wires are in 'b' holes and the LED and resistor are in 't' holes.
The blue strip is taken to be the 'bn' rail. Rail hole numbers are estimated from the picture. Wires go to bn.1, bn.25 and bn.19. The resistor goes to bn.10.
Button pin convention: '1' is the row j side, '2' is the row h side, 'l' is the left column and 'r' is the right column. Left button: columns 1 and 3. Right button: columns 28 and 30.
Wire ends: for pin-to-socket wires (jumper-wire-mf), port a is the male pin end into the breadboard and port b is the female socket end on the Pi header.
The LED short leg (cathode) is in column 15 with the resistor. The long leg (anode) is in column 16 with the GPIO4 wire, as in the image. The manual text says D15/D16 but the image shows row e.
The manual's resistor sentence says 'short leg of the resistor' but means the LED. The 330 ohm value comes from the parts list.
Each wire and lead gets a joined edge and an electrical edge to the same port.
